chunks: From him from his father from Ibn Sinan from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'fur from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
It did not happen that Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was saying for something which had transpired: 'If only something else would have happened'.

key_terms.لَوْ كَانَ غَيْرُهُ: If only something else would have happened

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet (peace be upon him) say about regretting past events?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi underscores the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) embodiment of *rida* (contentment) by avoiding 'if only' statements, a practice that Shia scholars cite as the ideal model for believers to accept divine decree without regret. It highlights that true satisfaction with Allah’s judgment is not merely passive acceptance but an active spiritual state reflecting deep trust in divine wisdom. This prophetic behavior serves as a practical guide for navigating life's events with equanimity and gratitude.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ibn Sinan, from Al Husayn Bin Al Mukhtar, from Abdullah in Abu Yafour,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It did not happen that Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> was saying for something which had transpired: ‘If only something else would have happened’’.
en.sarwar: 13. It is narrated from him from his father from ibn Sinan from al-Husayn ibn al- Muhtar from ‘Abd Allah ibn abu Ya’fur from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“The Messenger of Allah (a.s.) never said about something that had taken place, ‘Would that something else had happened.’”
